# Approved commit author and committer identities for this repository.
#
# This list distinguishes two categories:
#
# 1. Approved public authoring identities — personal-domain addresses that the
#    maintainer has explicitly decided to keep as public authoring identities.
#    These are NOT leaked personal data; they are intentional public identities
#    already present in the public history of all unbraind/pm-* repositories.
#    On 2026-07-21 the maintainer reaffirmed an earlier closed decision to
#    retain stefan@preu.at. A different, previously purged work address WAS
#    purged in 2026-07 and must never be re-added.
#
# 2. Approved service and noreply identities — automated bot and noreply
#    addresses that do not carry personal identity metadata.
#
# The identity audit gate (tests/identity_audit.rs) fails closed on any
# author or committer email not listed here. It scans every object in the LOCAL
# object store, so it covers unreachable (dangling) objects when the store holds
# them. In CI it does not: a clone never transfers server-side dangling objects,
# so a green CI run is evidence about refs and tags, not about the whole
# upstream object database. See README.md for the distinction.

# Approved public authoring identity (maintainer decision 2026-07-21).
stefan@preu.at

# The maintainer's GitHub noreply address.
unbraind@users.noreply.github.com

# The GitHub Actions bot noreply address used on automated push/merge refs.
1153461+unbraind@users.noreply.github.com

# GitHub's committer for merges made through the web UI.
noreply@github.com

# Dependabot's public GitHub noreply address on dependency pull-request refs.
49699333+dependabot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com
# The GitHub Actions bot, which authors the release commit created by
# .github/workflows/release.yml. It must be listed here: the first release would
# otherwise write a commit that this very audit rejects on every subsequent run.
41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com
